title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
description: Brute force to optimized: a frequency hash map versus single-pass run-detection that exploits the list already being sorted.

sections.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

content.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

blocks.text: Given the head of a SORTED linked list, delete all nodes that have duplicate numbers, leaving only distinct numbers from the original list. Return the resulting sorted list.

blocks.caption: Unlike the simpler "remove duplicates" variant, here EVERY node involved in a duplicate is removed, not just the extra copies

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","The head of a sorted singly linked list"],["Output","The head of the list with every node that had ANY duplicate completely removed, keeping only values that appeared exactly once"],["Goal","Remove entire duplicate runs (not just the extras) in a single pass"],["Constraints","The number of nodes is in the range [0, 300]; -100 <= Node.val <= 100; the list is already sorted in ascending order"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["The list is already SORTED","All duplicates of a value are guaranteed to be consecutive, so a single forward pass with a \"run-detection\" check suffices"],["A node with duplicates must be entirely REMOVED, including its very first occurrence (not just the later copies)","A dummy head is essential here, since the head itself might need to be removed, and prev must only advance past values confirmed to be unique"]]}

blocks.text: This differs from the simpler "remove duplicates, keep one copy" variant: here, if a value appears more than once anywhere in the list, EVERY node with that value is deleted, leaving none of them behind.

blocks.title: Analogy: Removing Every Person Who Shares a Birthday With Someone Else
blocks.text: Given a line of people sorted by birthday, remove EVERYONE who shares their birthday with at least one other person in the line, not just the "extra" duplicates. If three people share a birthday, all three leave; if a person's birthday is unique, they stay. Since the line is sorted by birthday, everyone sharing a birthday is guaranteed to stand next to each other, making it easy to spot an entire group at once.

blocks.caption: A run of equal values is detected and entirely skipped if its length exceeds 1; prev only advances past confirmed-unique nodes

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["Value 1: appears once","Kept","No duplicate"],["Value 2: appears once","Kept","No duplicate"],["Value 3: appears twice (a run of two 3s)","Both removed entirely","Any duplicate run is fully deleted, not just the extra copy"],["Value 4: appears twice","Both removed entirely","Same rule applied again"],["Value 5: appears once","Kept","No duplicate"],["Answer","[1,2,5]","Only the values that appeared exactly once survive"]]}

{"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["Value 1: appears three times","All three removed entirely, INCLUDING the very first node (the original head)","The entire run is a duplicate, regardless of position"],["Values 2 and 3: each appears once","Both kept","No duplicates"],["Answer","[2,3]","The head itself changes, since the original head (value 1) was part of a duplicate run"]]}

blocks.text: Before extracting values and manually recomputing frequency counts, notice that the list's SORTED property guarantees every duplicate run is a single, contiguous block, detectable in one linear pass.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Because the list is sorted, all occurrences of any given value are guaranteed to be immediately next to each other, forming one contiguous "run."

Observation 2: At each node, checking whether node.next exists AND has the same value as node reveals whether the CURRENT run has more than one element.

Observation 3: If a run has more than one element, ALL of it (starting from the current node) should be skipped entirely, advancing past every node sharing that value, until a different value (or the list's end) is reached.

Observation 4: A dummy head is essential here, since the very first run (potentially including the true head) might itself need to be entirely removed, which would otherwise require special-casing the head separately.

Observation 5: prev should only ever be advanced onto a node CONFIRMED to be part of a run of exactly one, since prev represents "the last node known to survive in the final result."
This is a single-pass "run-detection and skip" technique on a sorted list, using a dummy head to uniformly handle the case where even the original head must be removed.
Count the frequency of every value across the whole list, then keep only the values whose frequency is exactly 1.

items: Walk through the list once, building a frequency count of every value.
Walk through the list again (or the same collected values), keeping only those whose frequency is exactly 1.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: A hash map naturally counts frequencies regardless of whether duplicates happen to be adjacent, though here (since the list is sorted) they always are.
Filtering keeps only frequency-1 values, directly matching the "remove ALL duplicates entirely" requirement.

blocks.text: Correctly identifies and removes every value with more than one occurrence, regardless of the list being sorted or not.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), two linear passes.
Space: O(n), for the frequency hash map.
Limitation: the hash map is unnecessary given that the list is sorted; a single pass with direct run-detection achieves the same result in O(1) extra space.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force needs a full frequency map. Instead, since the list is sorted, walk through it once: at each node, check if the NEXT node shares its value. If so, skip past the ENTIRE run of matching values before reconnecting prev.next to whatever comes after. If not, the current node is confirmed unique, so prev simply advances onto it.

Use a dummy head with prev = dummy. Walk node through the list: if node.next exists and shares node's value, skip node forward past the entire matching run, then set prev.next = node (bypassing the whole run); otherwise, advance prev to node and node to node.next.
Detect each duplicate run directly (using the sorted property) and skip past it entirely in a single pass.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","node","Action","prev.next currently points to"],"rows":[["Start","1 (1st)","node.next (1) matches node.val (1): a run detected","dummy (unset)"],["Skip run","-","Advance node past all three 1s, until node = 2","-"],["Reconnect","2","prev.next = node (2), bypassing the entire run of 1s","2"],["Unique node","2","node.next (3) does not match node.val (2): unique, advance prev to 2","2"],["Unique node","3","node.next is null: unique, advance prev to 3","3"]]}

blocks.title: Final answer
blocks.text: The resulting list is [2,3], matching the expected result; the original head (value 1) was correctly removed entirely.

codes.python:
def delete_duplicates(head):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    prev = dummy
    node = head
    while node:
        if node.next and node.next.val == node.val:
            val = node.val
            while node and node.val == val:                                 # skip past the ENTIRE run of this duplicated value
                node = node.next
            prev.next = node                                                # prev connects directly to whatever comes after the run
        else:
            prev = node                                                     # a unique value: keep it, advance prev normally
            node = node.next
    return dummy.next


if __name__ == "__main__":
    head = ListNode(1, ListNode(1, ListNode(1, ListNode(2, ListNode(3)))))
    result = delete_duplicates(head)
    values = []
    while result:
        values.append(result.val)
        result = result.next
    print(values)

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), each node is visited a constant number of times overall.
Space: O(1) extra, reusing the existing nodes.

Because the list is sorted, checking only the IMMEDIATE next node for a matching value is sufficient to detect the start of a duplicate run; the inner while loop then correctly consumes the entire run (however long it is) before prev.next is reconnected. prev only ever advances onto nodes already confirmed to be part of a run of exactly one, guaranteeing the final result contains only truly unique values.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["A run of length 1 (unique value)","prev advances directly onto it, keeping it in the result"],["A run of length > 1","node skips past the entire run; prev.next is reconnected directly to whatever follows, removing the whole run"],["The duplicate run includes the original head","The dummy head lets this be handled uniformly, without any special-casing"]]}

items: The dummy head is essential, since dummy.next (not head directly) is what gets returned, correctly reflecting cases where the original head itself is removed.
The inner while loop (skipping the run) uses the SAME val variable captured before the loop starts, ensuring it correctly consumes every node sharing that exact value.
prev.next = node after skipping a run correctly reconnects, bypassing the entire removed run in one step.

blocks.text: On a SORTED list, duplicate values are always contiguous, so detecting and entirely skipping a run can be done directly in a single pass, avoiding any extra frequency-counting structure.

items: Forgetting the dummy head, which is required since the original head itself might be part of a duplicate run and need removing.
Advancing prev even when a duplicate run was just skipped, which would incorrectly leave prev pointing at a node that no longer exists in the intended result.
Confusing this problem with the simpler "keep one copy of each duplicate" variant, which uses a different (simpler) rule.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Edge case","Expected behavior"],"rows":[["Empty list","Returns null (dummy.next) immediately"],["Every node has the same value","The entire list is one giant duplicate run, so the result is an empty list"],["No duplicates at all","Every node is kept exactly as-is, since prev advances onto every node"]]}

items: Explicitly contrasting this problem with the simpler "Remove Duplicates from Sorted List" (keep one copy) variant clarifies the exact rule difference (remove entire runs vs. keep one representative) up front.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Delete ALL nodes with ANY duplicate" (not just extra copies) on a SORTED list points toward single-pass run-detection using a dummy head, since even the head might be removed.

items: How would this differ if the list were NOT sorted? Duplicates would no longer be guaranteed contiguous, requiring a frequency map (the brute force approach) instead of direct run-detection.

How would you solve the simpler variant (keep ONE copy of each duplicate value) instead? That requires only comparing each node to its immediate next node and skipping just the EXTRA copies, not the first occurrence.

Can this be done recursively instead of iteratively? Yes: recursively process the rest of the list first, then decide whether the current node (and its run) should be included based on whether it matches the next value.
A stricter variant of the simpler duplicate-removal problem elsewhere in this category, both relying on the sorted list guaranteeing that duplicates are always contiguous.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n) time, O(n) space.
Optimized (single-pass run-detection): O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: Pattern: Single-pass run-detection and skip, on a sorted list

Core Idea: Since duplicates are guaranteed contiguous, detect each run by comparing a node to its immediate next node, and entirely skip any run longer than 1, using a dummy head to uniformly handle head removal
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
Most Important Observation: prev must only ever advance onto nodes CONFIRMED to belong to a run of exactly one
Interview Difficulty: Medium
One-line memory trick: Dummy head; if node.next.val == node.val, skip the WHOLE run and reconnect prev.next, else advance prev normally
